method: Direct page opened through the current web browsing layer; article body inspected rather than relying on the failed command-line fetch.

observations.evidence: The DOJ page is dated September 8, 2026 and reports that James Strahler II was sentenced to 180 months for cybercrimes involving real and AI-generated sexually explicit images and threats.
The DOJ calls this the first U.S. prosecution/conviction under the Take It Down Act and says the publication-of-digital-forgeries conviction is part of that 2025 law.
The page lists three guilty-plea offences and describes harassment, threats, real and AI-generated images involving adult women and children.
The official page states it was updated September 8, 2026.

limitations: A prosecution press release is the government account, not a sentencing transcript or count-by-count allocation of the sentence.
The first-conviction claim remains attributed to the U.S. Attorney’s Office.
